messages:
incident-bot: Pager: P0 - runtime container crashloop on gw-rt-pool (severity: high). Affected service: runtime-serving. Error seen: SIGSEGV in /opt/runtime/lib/custom_kernels.so. Pods restarting across 3 nodes. @ryan (oncall) you have the pager.

ryan (oncall): got it. I'm pulling logs and will triage. tagging @sahil from runtime.

ryan (oncall): quick summary from kubectl describe -> CrashLoopBackOff with last state terminated: Signal: 11 (SIGSEGV). Restart count: 12. Nodes: gw-n1,gw-n2,gw-n3.

jen: saw node flapping a bit, some kernel messages earlier today but pretty stable until ~12:03 UTC. I'll check node-level OOM/kern logs.

sahil: thanks. attaching the last 40 lines from container stdout (trimmed):

```
[2026-03-15T12:03:10Z] initializing model cache
[2026-03-15T12:03:10Z] loading TRT engine: model_v2.trt
[2026-03-15T12:03:14Z] CUDA init ok, device 0: A100-SXM4
[2026-03-15T12:03:15Z] warming KV cache
[2026-03-15T12:03:16Z] runtime: launching worker pid=2145
[2026-03-15T12:03:17Z] ERROR: segfault at 0x7fffc1234 in custom_kernels::fused_attention
Received signal 11 (Segmentation fault)
#0  0x00007f9c2b1a3e9f in custom_kernels::fused_attention(cudaStream_t, ...)
#1  0x000055aa8b2f4b1c in runtime::KernelLauncher::run
#2  0x000055aa8b1d2340 in runtime::ModelExecutor::execute_batch
```

```
(gdb) bt
#0  fused_attention + 0x2f9
#1  KernelLauncher::run + 0x1cc
#2  ModelExecutor::execute_batch + 0x540
#3  start_thread
#4  clone
```

sahil: looks like crash inside our custom fused_attention in custom_kernels.so which wraps a TRT plugin. suspect a bad edge case in attention length handling.

luis: are we seeing CUDA errors or driver issues on the nodes? jen?

jen: checked dmesg on gw-n2 and gw-n3: repeated "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, PID=2145" around the same time. No OOM-kill at kernel level. driver version 535.x applied last week during rolling upgrade.

ryan (oncall): notes: this coincides with a canary model rollout at 11:55 UTC (deploy-bot also posted). Could be a model+kernel incompat. deploy-bot, can you confirm what image/tag rolled?

deploy-bot: New image pushed: runtime:v2026.3.15-canary-7f2c. Rollout to 10% started at 11:55 UTC. No auto-rollback yet.

sahil: hmm that canary image includes a rebuilt custom_kernels.so with a modified fused kernel to support longer prefix lengths. Trying to reproduce locally with same driver.

ryan (oncall): mitigation options: 1) scale the service down to reduce customer impact, 2) rollback canary to previous image, 3) cordon/drain affected nodes, 4) temporary routing to older model variant. Thoughts?

maya: Customer impact: two enterprise customers on dedicated clusters reported elevated error rates and latency spikes starting at 12:04 UTC. CS is preparing notices. We should avoid broad rollback if we can failover traffic.

luis: high risk to keep the canary active. If it's segfaulting on device, could take nodes out of rotation. My recommendation: roll back canary and drain nodes showing repeated Xid.

sahil: I agree. Reproduced locally with driver 535.33 and TRT 8.5. Crash reproduces when sequence_length > 8192 due to an unguarded pointer in fused_attention. Patch incoming. But patch needs CI and image rebuild.

ryan (oncall): immediate action: rollback canary to runtime:v2026.3.14-stable across all clusters. jen, can you start draining gw-n2 for deeper node-level inspection after rollback? luis, coordinate draining. sahil, assemble a hotfix image build. maya, I'll escalate customer comms.

jen: starting drain on gw-n2 now (kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data). Will monitor pod reschedules.

deploy-bot: Rollback triggered by @ryan (oncall): deploying runtime:v2026.3.14-stable to canary slice. Progress: 0/12 pods updated.

(2m later)

deploy-bot: Rollback progress: 9/12 pods updated. CrashLoop rate down to 1 pod.

sahil: building hotfix branch 'fix/fused-attn-bounds' and running quick unit tests. Will push image runtime:v2026.3.15-hotfix-1 when green.

luis: gw-n2 logs show Xid errors stopped after rollback on that node. gw-n3 still has one restart. recommending we cordon gw-n3 and rotate workloads there to safe nodes while root cause confirmed.

ryan (oncall): cordon gw-n3 and move pods off. jen, proceed.

jen: cordoned gw-n3 (kubectl cordon gw-n3). Evicting pods now.

(10m later)

deploy-bot: New image built by sahil: runtime:v2026.3.15-hotfix-1 pushed to registry. Canary deploy scheduled.

sahil: hotfix addresses bounds check in fused_attention and adds defensive cudaGetLastError checks. Patch diff: +if (seq_len > MAX_SEQ) { return error; } +cudaPeekAtLastError assertions.

ryan (oncall): canary the hotfix to 5% first. If stable for 10m with no restarts, we'll ramp.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout: runtime:v2026.3.15-hotfix-1 -> 5% started.

(8m monitoring)

deploy-bot: Canary: 0 crashes observed in canary slice for 8 minutes. Pod restarts stable.

luis: nodes gw-n2/gw-n3 show no new Xid messages in dmesg since the rollback and cordon. Good.

sahil: running a smoke test sampling sequence lengths up to 16384 against canary. No segfaults so far.

maya: CS update: sent interim note to affected customers explaining we rolled back the canary and expect a staged hotfix deploy. Offering SLA credits if customers want.

ryan (oncall): next steps: 1) Ramp hotfix to 50% after 15m stable, 2) schedule full rollout if no regressions, 3) prepare postmortem: timeline, root cause (bounds check in custom fused kernel), and action items (add seq_len fuzz tests, add canary test with long sequences, add driver compatibility matrix).

sahil: will open PR with regression tests and include a small reproducer harness for CI that runs long-seq paths under emulated driver.

jen: after hotfix rollout we should rejoin gw-n3 to the pool and watch for Xid. I'll keep nodes cordoned until we validate.

luis: putting incident into "monitoring" state. Please add any additional notes here.

ryan (oncall): handing off to @luis for post-deploy monitoring. I'm going offline for a bit but will join the follow-up postmortem. good job team. :thumbsup:

luis: acknowledged. I'll collect logs and begin the incident write-up template. tagging @sahil @jen for attachments.

incident-bot: Incident updated: state -> monitoring. Incident duration so far: 45 minutes. Pager cleared for @ryan (oncall).

(END)
